summary: The pack is internally coherent with the frozen security v3 joins on every rule I own (handles per grant with both tokens, host-internal locator, nonblocking lease handoff under the fence, report-only doctor, metadata-only help/version, four-class fleet with per-class G13, effective policy with deny-by-absence). The supersessions are quoted by heading and item, which lands my audit's C1 resolution. One join has no home in the foundation's closed root layout, and four references are stale or under-specified.

mustFix.where: section 1, the sentence 'The root contains lifecycle.sqlite, trust.sqlite, lifecycle.lock, generations/, staging/, quarantine/, projects/<namespaceId>/, settings.json, policies/permission-policy.json, and cache/' and the following custody sentences
mustFix.defect: The closed root layout has no location for the per-spawn result scratch root that distribution section 8 consumes ('the bounded scratch-root/commit-class bootstrap metadata and typed byte courier') and security v3 section 7.5 requires ('host-created per spawn by mkdirat under the held operational-root fd, mode 0700, a fresh name per spawn ... under the per-user operational root'). staging/ is generation publication and cache/ is deletable acceleration; neither may hold HE-1 stage bytes or HE-2 results. As frozen, the courier is homeless in the layout the pack calls complete.
mustFix.evidenceToResolve: Add to the layout: 'projects/<namespaceId>/spawns/<spawnId>/ holds one spawn's result scratch root (security v3 section 7.5): created 0700 by the operation holding that project's operation lease, named to the worker only through the bootstrap successor member, removed at spawn end; never a retention root, never a generation or cache path, excluded from G02 mandatory-path measurement; garbage collection may remove a spawn directory only after the census proves its operation lease released.' State that cache deletion cannot reach it.

shouldFix.defect: The sibling subject distribution-runtime-completion.v1.md section 3 concretizes the lock shape 'as concretized in component-lock-schema.completed.v3.json' (registryViewDigest, selectedCompatibility, scopeContext), and g15-conditional-contract.v2.md states that v3 retains the reviewed v2 grammar. The matrix pins the superseded v2 file; two subjects of one frozen pack name different lock grammars.
shouldFix.evidenceToResolve: Set lockGrammar to component-lock-schema.completed.v3.json (or state explicitly that the matrix pins the v2 grammar which v3 retains and name v3 as the current lock shape).

shouldFix.where: section 10, sentence beginning '`compatibility-matrix.completed.v3.json` supersedes only v2's illustrative exact initial host constraint'
shouldFix.defect: The pinned subject is compatibility-matrix.completed.v4.json (sections 3 and 8.1 say v4 adds S-DOCTOR). Section 10 makes a claim about bytes not in the unit (v3) and leaves the v3-to-v4 step unstated in the supersession trail.
shouldFix.evidenceToResolve: Rewrite as: 'compatibility-matrix.completed.v4.json supersedes v2's illustrative exact initial host constraint with the patch-compatible interval above (first made in v3) and adds S-DOCTOR (section 8.1); v2's separation of release and state remains.'

shouldFix.where: section 3, 'resolutionInputs adds the current public `permissionPolicyDigest`, which identifies policy bytes, never consent or a grant'
shouldFix.defect: Under the frozen security v3 section 6.11 the lock's permissionPolicyDigest is the domain digest (opensip.metadata.policy-effective.1) of the effective document, which embeds both raw-file digests; it never equals any raw file's bytes. 'identifies policy bytes' invites a reader (and the pending G15 bridge) to pin one raw file, which is exactly the 'whichever was last' ambiguity the foundation's two-file carrier creates.
shouldFix.evidenceToResolve: Replace with: 'resolutionInputs adds the current permissionPolicyDigest: the effective-policy document digest of security v3 section 6.11, which pins both private raw sources and their merge; it identifies policy, never consent or a grant.'

shouldFix.file: host-foundation-completion.v1.md (section 1) and distribution-runtime-completion.v1.md (section 5, project_selection(projectKey, generationId) and project_registry)
shouldFix.where: the sentences 'NamespaceId is the immutable lifecycle UUID, never projectKey bytes. A project namespace owns its grant-journal.sqlite, operation-lock files, local permission policy and registry-view exports' and 'per-project journals live in the host-owned project state namespace'
shouldFix.defect: Three project identities now coexist: the lifecycle projectKey (selection key), the foundation namespaceId (directory name) and the security locator's projectKeyDigest (host-internal locator and witness carrier identity). The pack never says which row joins them, so an implementer cannot tell whether a witness that names projectKeyDigest belongs to projects/<namespaceId>/.
shouldFix.evidenceToResolve: Add one joining sentence (the lead offered to repair on v2 paths): 'The project_registry row binds projectKey, namespaceId and the security locator identity projectKeyDigest = SHA-256(projectKey UTF-8) for one root identity; the grant journal and its witness live at projects/<namespaceId>/ and name their carrier by projectKeyDigest and grantGeneration; no path is derived from projectKey bytes or from that digest.'

advisories.note: 'Required TCB verification helpers are separate processes with their own signed closure' is compatible with security v3 section 8.3 but should say the macOS Security.framework helper is qualification-only, never a launch-path or G02-mandatory member, so the G02 accounting and the launch-verification classes stay consistent.

'Handles arrive through the declared structural environment' is right; consider naming the bootstrap successor member (resultScratchRoot) once the broker SDK unit freezes, so the reference does not read as if the frozen bootstrap v2 already carries the courier's root.

The three harness occupancies named are specifications, not executed corpora (legacy-corpus-checker-audit.v1); label them design evidence or point at the retained doctor/cache checker report so the matrix does not imply executed evidence.
